h1: The 6 Best 50 Ft Halloween Lights of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best 50 Ft Halloween Lights: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 Halloween light strings at 50 feet scored on weather rating, bulb type, color mix, connectability and price.
summary: The IP65 50FT Halloween String Lights Outdoor is the best pick for a porch that gets real weather, since it states a waterproof rating and shatterproof plastic. The SUNSGNE G40 is the better choice if you want orange and purple globes with replaceable E12 bulbs. The 25-bulb orange, green and purple set adds color variety, while the CXLHO is the cheapest way to cover 50 feet.
intro: The word 50 ft on a Halloween light listing is the most misleading number in the category. It is usually the length of the strand, not the lit length, and the first and last bulbs can sit a foot or more from each end. Buy one strand for a 50-foot porch run and you may end up stapling a dark gap above the door.

So we ranked these six 50-foot strings by what holds up outdoors: a stated weather rating, shatterproof or replaceable bulbs, the way strands connect end to end and the color mix. We reviewed only listings that state a 50-foot length, leaving out shorter strings, and scored each on the Primea framework.

products.name: 50FT Halloween String Lights Outdoor
products.verdict: A 50-foot string with an IP65 waterproof rating and shatterproof plastic bulbs.
products.description:
This string lists IP65 waterproof and all-weather durability, plus shatterproof plastic that the listing calls safe for kids and pets. IP65 means the string is sealed against dust and low-pressure water jets, which is the practical standard for lights that hang on a porch through rain and wind.

It leads the ranking because it is the only strand here to state a recognized weather rating. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no bulb count, base type or color mix in the specs, so you must check those on the page. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, with the other premium strings.

Buy it for a porch or patio that sees weather. Skip it if you want replaceable bulbs.
products.idealFor: Porches and patios that see rain and wind.
products.skipIf: You want to swap bulbs or choose a color mix.

products.name: SUNSGNE G40 LED Halloween String Lights Outdoor 50FT Halloween Globe Lights
products.verdict: G40 globe lights on an E12 base in orange and purple, with plugs at both ends.
products.description:
The SUNSGNE is a 50-foot set of G40 globe bulbs on an E12 base in orange and purple. A standard E12 candelabra base means a dead bulb can be replaced from a hardware store, rather than throwing out the whole string, and each set has male and female plugs so you can link strands.

It ranks second because it gives no weather rating, which the top string does state. It is shatterproof and energy saving, and it also sits in the $25 to $50 bucket. The globe shape gives a party-lights look that suits patios more than eaves.

Buy it for a yard or fence line where you want classic globe lights. Skip it if you need a documented waterproof rating.
pros: Male and female plugs for linking
products.idealFor: Patios and fence lines wanting a party-light look.
products.skipIf: You need a stated weather rating.

products.name: 50FT Halloween String Lights with 25 G40 LED Orange Green Purple Bulbs
products.verdict: A 50-foot string of 25 G40 bulbs in orange, green and purple.
products.description:
This 50-foot strand carries 25 G40 LED bulbs in orange, green and purple, which works out to a bulb about every two feet. Three colors give a more traditional Halloween palette than the two-color sets, with the green adding a witchy contrast.

It places third because the listing says little about weather protection or replaceable bulbs, and a 25-bulb count means wider spacing than the 200-light CXLHO. It does use heavy-duty construction and end-to-end male and female plugs, in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It suits a yard or porch where you want color variety and bold bulbs. Skip it if you want a dense, glowing wash of light.
products.idealFor: Yards wanting bold bulbs in three classic colors.
products.skipIf: You want dense, even light along the strand.

products.name: C9 Purple Halloween String Lights
products.verdict: A 50-foot C9 purple string with clear spacing and replaceable E17 bulbs.
products.description:
The C9 set is a 50-foot purple string with clear spacing between bulbs and replaceable E17 bulbs. C9 is the old-fashioned large Christmas-style bulb, and its bigger shape reads well from the street, while the replaceable E17 base means one failed bulb does not end the string.

It sits fourth because it comes in one color, purple, and the listing gives no weather rating. Next to the SUNSGNE, it trades the globe look for a more traditional roofline style, and it costs the same $25 to $50.

A good fit for outlining eaves, railings and windows. Skip it if you want orange or multicolor.
products.idealFor: Eaves, railings and windows needing a roofline look.
products.skipIf: You want orange or a color mix.

products.name: Abeja 50FT G40 Purple Halloween String Lights
products.verdict: Purple G40 globes with shatterproof LED bulbs and low heat.
products.description:
The Abeja string offers purple G40 globe lights, 50 feet long, with shatterproof LED bulbs and an energy-saving, low-heat design. Low heat is a real advantage on a Halloween display that sits against fabric, foam props or dried leaves, since LEDs stay cool where incandescents do not.

Fifth place follows from overlap with the SUNSGNE G40, which offers similar globes but in a single color, and the listing gives no base type or connection detail. It also lacks a stated weather rating. It costs $25 to $50.

Buy it for a purple-themed display with props nearby. Skip it if you need to link strings or want a color mix.
products.idealFor: Purple-themed displays near props and fabric.
products.skipIf: You want to link strings or mix colors.

products.name: CXLHO Christmas Mini String Lights Orange
products.verdict: A 50-foot, 200-count orange mini string that connects end to end, for under $25.
products.description:
The CXLHO lists 50 feet with 200 orange mini bulbs, end-to-end connectable, for Halloween and fall decor. Mini lights are small, so 200 of them pack a bulb every three inches or so, giving a continuous glow instead of the dotted look of bigger globes.

It ranks last because the product name says Christmas and the listing mentions no weather rating or shatterproof bulbs, so it is the least targeted to outdoor Halloween use. It does cost under $25, the lowest bucket here, and it links to extend the run.

Choose it for wrapping trees, garlands and railings on a budget. Skip it for a harsh weather exposure.
products.idealFor: Budget wrapping of trees, garlands and railings.
products.skipIf: The lights will face heavy rain or wind.

whatMatters.detail: An IP rating tells you how well the string resists water and dust. IP65 handles rain and spray, while a plain outdoor label proves little. Look for the IP number in the listing, as on the 50FT Halloween String Lights Outdoor, and keep connection points off the ground where water pools.

Globe G40, large C9 and mini bulbs light very differently. Globes give a party look, C9 bulbs suit rooflines, and minis give a dense glow. Check the bulb name in the title, then think about how it will look from the street, where small bulbs fade and large ones read clearly.

A string with a standard E12 or E17 base lets you swap a dead bulb, while sealed strings must be discarded. Look for a base type in the listing, as on the SUNSGNE and C9 sets, and keep a few spare bulbs. A single failed bulb is a nuisance on a sealed string.

End-to-end plugs let you link strands for a longer run, but every string has a maximum number of connections on one circuit. Check the listing for the connection limit, as the G40 sets mention, and avoid chaining more than the label allows, since overloaded strings run hot.

The stated 50 feet is usually the entire strand, including the lead wire and plug end. The lit portion may be several feet shorter. Measure your run first, then check the listing for lead length and add a short extension cord if the outlet is far from the display.

faq.q: Can I link several 50 ft strings together?
faq.a: Often yes. The SUNSGNE, the 25-bulb G40 set and the CXLHO list end-to-end plugs, but every string has a connection limit. Read the label before chaining, because exceeding it can overheat the wiring on a single outlet.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with outdoor Halloween lights?
faq.a: Buying a string without a weather rating and leaving the plug on wet ground. Only the 50FT Halloween String Lights Outdoor states IP65. Raise connections on a hook or in a weatherproof cover, whichever string you choose.

faq.q: Are G40 globes worth it over the CXLHO mini lights?
faq.a: For visibility, yes. G40 globes in the SUNSGNE and Abeja strings read clearly from the street, while the CXLHO packs 200 small bulbs for an even glow at close range. Choose minis for trees and globes for fences.

faq.q: How do I hang a 50-foot string?
faq.a: Plan the run before unrolling, and use clips or hooks every foot or two. On the C9 Purple string, space the clips to keep bulbs upright. Put the plug end nearest the outlet so you avoid extension cord gaps.

faq.q: How do I store Halloween lights?
faq.a: Wind each string loosely around a cardboard tube or reel, tape the plug end to the roll and store it dry. Keep spare E12 or E17 bulbs from the SUNSGNE and C9 sets in a labelled bag with the string.

faq.q: Are LED Halloween lights safe around props?
faq.a: Generally, since LEDs run cool. The Abeja G40 string lists low heat and shatterproof bulbs, which suits foam props and fabric. Still keep plugs and connections clear of dry leaves, and unplug the display when you are away.

finalTake: The 50FT Halloween String Lights Outdoor is the best pick here because it states an IP65 rating and uses shatterproof plastic. The SUNSGNE G40 is the smart alternative for globe lights with replaceable E12 bulbs, and the C9 Purple suits eaves. The CXLHO is the budget option for sheltered trees and garlands. Measure the run, check the connection limit and keep plugs off wet ground.
